questions.question: Why can naive softmax fail on logits [1000, 1001], and what is the stable remedy?
options: exp overflows; subtract the maximum logit before exponentiating
The logits are negative; add their minimum before exponentiating
Softmax requires integer logits; round them first
Division by the sum always creates underflow, so use raw logits
questions.explanation: The probabilities are unchanged by a common shift. Subtracting 1001 produces [-1,0], keeping exponentials in a safe range.

questions.question: Which expression is a stable log-sum-exp calculation for values x?
options: log(sum(exp(x_i))) without any shift
m + log(sum(exp(x_i - m))) where m=max(x)
sum(log(x_i)) divided by len(x)
max(x) * log(sum(x_i))
questions.explanation: Factoring out the largest value prevents overflow: log(sum exp x) = m + log(sum exp(x-m)).

questions.question: A centered finite-difference gradient becomes noisy when h is reduced from 1e-5 to 1e-12. What is the likely cause?
options: The analytical derivative has become discontinuous by definition
A smaller h always increases floating-point precision
Subtraction cancellation and rounding error dominate the tiny numerator
The function has changed from scalar to vector
questions.explanation: f(x+h) and f(x-h) become nearly equal at tiny h, so their subtraction loses significant digits. A moderate step balances truncation and roundoff error.

questions.question: Why is bfloat16 often safer than float16 for training activations?
options: It has more mantissa bits than float32
It stores every number exactly
It removes the need for loss scaling in every model
It has a wider exponent range, reducing overflow and underflow
questions.explanation: bfloat16 keeps float32's exponent width but uses fewer fraction bits. Its range is therefore much wider than float16's, even though its precision is lower.

questions.question: Data values are around 1e8 with tiny variation. Which variance method avoids E[x^2] - E[x]^2 cancellation?
options: Use the one-pass Welford update
Square the already rounded mean again
Subtract the largest value from every label only at the end
Use a smaller integer type
questions.explanation: Welford's online updates maintain a stable running mean and sum of squared deviations instead of subtracting two huge, nearly equal quantities.

questions.question: A gradient vector has norm 20 and clip_by_norm receives max_norm=5. What should it return?
options: The vector scaled by 20/5
The vector scaled by 5/20
A vector of all zeros regardless of its direction
The original vector with each component clipped to 5
questions.explanation: Norm clipping preserves direction and scales only when the norm exceeds the limit. Here the returned norm is 5.
